text:
- chief complaint: the patient reports exercise-induced asthma symptoms, including difficulty breathing during sports (water polo) requiring them to stop, and worsening low mood.
- history of present illness: the patient has asthma and uses albuterol as needed, mainly during aerobic activity, with symptoms of phlegm, chest tightness, wheezing, and lightheadedness that improve partially with inhaler use. Symptoms are triggered by smoke exposure as well. The patient has had new, increasing stress and sadness since the start of the year, linked to academic pressure (SATs, AP classes), with low motivation, withdrawal from friends, and fatigue.
- physical examination: heart, lungs, stomach, eyes, mouth, throat, reflexes, and palpation are normal; fluid is seen in the ears; no tonsils are present.
- symptoms experienced by the patient: exercise-induced wheezing, chest tightness, phlegm, lightheadedness, tremor after albuterol use, sadness, low motivation, fatigue, and possible seasonal allergies.
- new medications prescribed or changed, including dosages: montelukast (Singulair) started daily; dosage N/A. Albuterol continued as needed.
- follow-up instructions: return in about six weeks to assess asthma response; begin therapy for mood, complete screening questionnaires, and follow up in a couple of weeks.
